 WHAT TO EXPECT: Fall storm to soak Arizona with rain, flooding risk this weekend
 Friday and Sunday are ABC15 Weather Action Days as rain impacts the Valley 
 Prev 
 Next 
 By: 
 Geneva Zoltek , Amber Sullins , Jorge Torres 
 Posted 
 and last updated 
 Share Copy link Facebook Nextdoor X Threads Reddit LinkedIn Email WhatsApp Messenger Print 
 Add ABC15 as a Google Preferred Source 
 Big changes are on the way to Arizona as our next fall storm moves in.
 This storm will bring two rounds of rain to Arizona, one on Friday and one on Sunday. 
 A few storms on Friday could turn strong to severe, mainly across southern and central Arizona. Damaging winds and hail are the main threats through early evening.
 Flood Watches are in effect Friday and late Saturday night through Sunday for much of Arizona, including the Valley.
 Thankfully, it looks like Saturday will be a bit of a lull in between those rounds of rain. Early trick-or-treaters should stay mostly dry. Rain chances climb through the evening, so keep the rain gear handy if you’re out late.
 The Valley could see 1 to 2 inches of rain on Friday and Sunday combined. Some spots across the high country, especially along and below the Mogollon Rim, could pick up 2 to 3 inches of rain or more.
 Sunday’s rain will fall on already soaked ground from Friday, so the flooding risk will be higher.
 With impacts to outdoor activities and the potential to see areas of flooding, Friday and Sunday will be ABC15 Weather Action Days .
 Take action now to get ready for these weather changes and do not attempt to drive through any flooded areas.
 There’s still a slight chance for lingering showers on Monday, then the forecast will start to dry out again.
 This storm will bring a big dose of cool air, too. Valley highs drop into the mid to upper 70s Friday and Saturday, then down into the low 70s Sunday and Monday. This time of year, average highs are in the mid-80s.
